name: Penicillin mould (Penicillium chrysogenum)
short_description: Filamentous green mould built from septate hyaline hyphae. Erect conidiophores branch into metulae and flask-shaped phialides that pinch off unbranched chains of green conidia - the little brush (penicillus) that names the genus. It secretes penicillin to keep competing bacteria at a distance, and Alexander Fleming's accidental sighting of that bacteria-free zone in 1928 became the first antibiotic.

textbook.1: PASS - muted, sophisticated educational palette with thin clean outlines exactly in the rod-bacterium/parasite house style. A mat of pale ivory SEPTATE hyphae with clearly drawn darker cross-walls runs along the bottom; one hypha rises as a long hyaline stalk with its own septa and, crucially, does NOT swell at the apex but branches into rami, then pale-sage metulae, then whorls of warm-cream flask-shaped phialides, each pinching off ONE long unbranched chain of sage-green conidia so the head fans out as an unmistakable paintbrush. A few loose conidia drift beside it. No Aspergillus vesicle, no sporangium, no mushroom, no yeast cell, no text, dark charcoal background edge-to-edge. Generous negative space around every structure. Chosen as label base.

sem.1: PASS - photorealistic false-colour SEM of a SINGLE conidiophore: straw-to-bronze stalk with faint constrictions at the cross-walls rising from slender surface hyphae, branching without any vesicle into metulae and phialides, and long unbranched chains of smooth ~3 um sage-green conidia splaying outward, the outermost chains softening in shallow depth of field and one chain visibly beginning to break apart. Surface only, no internal structures (correct for SEM), no text, no border, dark charcoal background.

3d.1: PASS - natural biological tints, not neon and not near-monochrome: translucent ivory stalk and hyphal mat with subsurface scattering and brown septal rings, pale-sage metulae, warm-cream ampulliform phialides and blue-green conidia in unbranched chains, plus a few free spores. Apex branches with no swollen vesicle. Soft global illumination and gentle rim light on a clean seamless dark studio background filling the frame; no text, no border.

watercolor.1: PASS - warm aged paper fills the whole square corner-to-corner with only a soft pale wash halo behind the subject; no mat, frame, drop-shadow or sheet-on-a-surface. Clearly COLOURED rather than sepia: ochre-cream stalk and hyphae with fine brown ink linework and drawn septa, pale-sage metulae, cream flask-shaped phialides and blue-green conidia in unbranched chains fanning out as a brush, with three loose spores drifting on the paper. No vesicle, no sporangium, no props, no text.

reference: PASS - Wikimedia Commons light micrograph of a lactophenol-cotton-blue tease mount (Ajay Kumar Chaurasiya, CC BY-SA 4.0) genuinely shows Penicillium: an erect stipe branching at its apex into deep-blue metulae and phialides with long UNBRANCHED chains of round conidia radiating outward, and NO swollen vesicle - so it is Penicillium and not Aspergillus. The original was a wider field with a second partial brush head, out-of-focus debris and scattered loose spore clusters, so it was cleaned with edit_image.py (real-02) to isolate ONE complete conidiophore on a uniform mount, keeping the LPCB colorization and the specimen's shape unchanged. HONEST CAVEAT: the source identifies the specimen to GENUS (Penicillium sp.), not to species - it is not independently confirmed as P. chrysogenum. That limitation is unavoidable here: P. chrysogenum and its sibling P. rubens are indistinguishable by light microscopy and can only be separated by sequencing, so no light micrograph could honestly claim species-level identity. Species-labelled alternatives exist (Bontemps CC BY 4.0, Ninjatacoshell CC BY-SA 3.0) but are visibly weaker - low contrast, heavy field vignette or an out-of-focus conidial mass - and were kept as backups in section 2.
decision: the clearest plate of the brush architecture: septate hyphae, stalk, rami, metulae, phialides and unbranched conidial chains all separable and labelled
false-colour surface-only SEM; single conidiophore, chains readable, closely matches the real micrograph
natural biological tints with translucent hyphae and pigmented conidia; labelled
full-bleed aged-paper naturalist plate, coloured washes over fine ink linework; labelled with black-on-paper ink
